indicator_or_finding: Stronger climate worry associated with lower fertility intentions, primarily childless people intending to forgo childbearing; weaker in Sweden.
limitations: No national percentage refusing children provided here; association not causation; country N not extracted.
study_title: Climate change worries and fertility intentions: Insights from three EU countries

indicator_or_finding: Stronger climate worry associated with lower fertility intentions, primarily childless people intending to forgo childbearing; weaker in Sweden.
limitations: No national percentage refusing children provided here; association not causation; country N not extracted.
study_title: Climate change worries and fertility intentions: Insights from three EU countries

indicator_or_finding: Stronger climate worry associated with lower fertility intentions, primarily childless people intending to forgo childbearing; weaker in Sweden.
limitations: No national percentage refusing children provided here; association not causation; country N not extracted.
study_title: Climate change worries and fertility intentions: Insights from three EU countries

indicator_or_finding: Climate change perceived as a problem associated with lower intentions to have a child.
limitations: Cross-sectional association, not percentage refusing children because of climate. Sample includes parents and childless people. Article prose has ambiguous labels for predicted-probability reference category; those percentages not transcribed.
study_title: Climate change concerns and fertility intentions: first evidence from Italy

indicator_or_finding: High climate worry associated with lower likelihood of having children in panel analysis; not proof of conscious climate-based refusal.
limitations: Observational longitudinal association; no percentage choosing childlessness inferred.
study_title: Personal and social worries associated with the likelihood of having children

indicator_or_finding: Reported to a high degree having fewer or no children as climate action
unit: percent of respondents finding item applicable
limitations: Denominator is only 72% of total sample who said item applicable; includes fewer children, not just none; self-report not observed birth suppression.
study_title: Attitudes towards childbearing, population, and the environment: prevalence, correlates, and connections with fertility outcomes in Sweden

indicator_or_finding: Climate worry not associated with current number of children, general ideal family size, or childbearing intentions in adjusted models.
population: GGS respondents aged 18–59; intentions asked of eligible subset
limitations: Different sample and analysis from CCP; cross-sectional associations; response rate 27%.
study_title: Attitudes towards childbearing, population, and the environment

indicator_or_finding: Climate concerns about potential children reported; climate change not ranked highly among other reproductive-choice factors.
population: Young, educated, climate-alarmed or climate-concerned Chinese
limitations: Purposively selected exploratory sample, not national estimate; child-welfare concern does not equal refusal.
study_title: The reproductive climate concerns of young, educated Chinese: when the nest is upset, no egg is left intact

indicator_or_finding: Climate-change awareness weakly negatively correlated with fertility desire.
population: Married women without children; convenience sample at public hospital in western Türkiye
limitations: Not nationally generalizable or causal; 95.5% planned children; awareness is broader than anxiety; fertility-desire scale reliability alpha=0.66. Article has internal reporting inconsistencies.
study_title: Climate Change Awareness: Does It Affect the Fertility Desire?

indicator_or_finding: Interviews explore environmental childlessness: reducing ecological footprint and concern for future child welfare.
limitations: Extracted from 2023 systematic-review Table 1, not independently rechecked primary text. Purposive/local qualitative evidence cannot estimate country prevalence.
study_title: Environmental Childlessness? Reproduction and (Im)Possible Futures amidst Environmental Crises

indicator_or_finding: Interviews with environmentally childfree participants identify ecological impacts and uncertain future as motivations.
limitations: Extracted from 2023 systematic-review Table 1, not independently rechecked primary text. Purposive/local qualitative evidence cannot estimate country prevalence.
study_title: There Are Many People Like Me, Who Feel They Want To Do Something Bigger

indicator_or_finding: Six of seven said climate change had already or may affect reproductive decisions; not all refused children.
population: British Columbia; nulliparous participants assigned female at birth, ages 18–25
limitations: Extracted from 2023 systematic-review Table 1, not independently rechecked primary text. Purposive/local qualitative evidence cannot estimate country prevalence.
study_title: Pregnancy Intentions of Youth in the Era of Climate Change: A Qualitative Auto-Photography Study

indicator_or_finding: Drought-related livelihood insecurity led some to desire smaller families; others saw children as household support.
population: 145 focus-group participants; 20 in-depth interviews; 16 stakeholder interviews
limitations: Extracted from 2023 systematic-review Table 1, not independently rechecked primary text. Purposive/local qualitative evidence cannot estimate country prevalence.
study_title: Burnt by the scorching sun: climate-induced livelihood transformations, reproductive health, and fertility trajectories in drought-affected communities of Zambia

indicator_or_finding: Climate adaptation and resource constraints linked to preferences for smaller families; not necessarily no children.
population: 96 focus-group participants; 42 interviews with community members, leaders and policymakers
limitations: Extracted from 2023 systematic-review Table 1, not independently rechecked primary text. Purposive/local qualitative evidence cannot estimate country prevalence.
study_title: Linking Population, Fertility, and Family Planning with Adaptation to Climate Change: Perspectives from Ethiopia

indicator_or_finding: Interviewees described future-child welfare, overconsumption and overpopulation as motivations for remaining childfree.
population: 24 interviewees pooled across NZ (Auckland/Christchurch) and US (Tucson); separate content analysis of 1,157 reader comments
limitations: Secondary extraction from review; n=24 is pooled, not each country. No country-specific prevalence.
study_title: No future, no kids–no kids, no future? An exploration of motivations to remain childfree in times of climate change

indicator_or_finding: Interviewees described future-child welfare, overconsumption and overpopulation as motivations for remaining childfree.
population: 24 interviewees pooled across NZ (Auckland/Christchurch) and US (Tucson); separate content analysis of 1,157 reader comments
limitations: Secondary extraction from review; n=24 is pooled, not each country. No country-specific prevalence.
study_title: No future, no kids–no kids, no future? An exploration of motivations to remain childfree in times of climate change

indicator_or_finding: Environmental and pollution-related health concern associated with less favorable reproductive attitudes; pollution concern correlated with lower child-number intentions.
limitations: Secondary extraction from systematic review; broader environment/pollution not climate-specific refusal; student sample not national.
study_title: Environmental concern and fertility intentions among Canadian university students

indicator_or_finding: General environmental concern associated with less favorable reproductive attitudes; egoistic/altruistic and biospheric concerns showed different directions.
limitations: Secondary extraction from systematic review; broader environment/pollution not climate-specific refusal; student sample not national.
study_title: The Problem of Overpopulation: Proenvironmental Concerns and Behavior Predict Reproductive Attitudes

indicator_or_finding: General environmental concern associated with less favorable attitudes toward having children.
limitations: Thesis included by systematic review; secondary extraction; not percentage refusing children or climate-specific measure.
study_title: Attitudes towards having Children in View of Climate Change

indicator_or_finding: Climate concern linked to lower ideal family size for families generally.
population: Ages 18–45; total n across four countries
limitations: Secondary extraction; n is pooled, not country N; ideal family size is not a decision to remain childfree; preserve differing outcome definitions.
study_title: Climate Change Concerns and the Ideal Number of Children: A Comparative Analysis of the V4 Countries

indicator_or_finding: Mixed results: direction differed between general family ideals and personal reproductive intentions.
population: Ages 18–45; total n across four countries
limitations: Secondary extraction; n is pooled, not country N; ideal family size is not a decision to remain childfree; preserve differing outcome definitions.
study_title: Climate Change Concerns and the Ideal Number of Children: A Comparative Analysis of the V4 Countries

indicator_or_finding: Only weak evidence of positive association with increased personal reproductive intentions in review; not clear climate-based refusal.
population: Ages 18–45; total n across four countries
limitations: Secondary extraction; n is pooled, not country N; ideal family size is not a decision to remain childfree; preserve differing outcome definitions.
study_title: Climate Change Concerns and the Ideal Number of Children: A Comparative Analysis of the V4 Countries

indicator_or_finding: Included in comparative study; no significant country-specific relationship highlighted in review summary.
population: Ages 18–45; total n across four countries
limitations: Secondary extraction; n is pooled, not country N; ideal family size is not a decision to remain childfree; preserve differing outcome definitions.
study_title: Climate Change Concerns and the Ideal Number of Children: A Comparative Analysis of the V4 Countries

indicator_or_finding: Review reports no significant association at alpha=.05 between climate concern and additionally intended children; weak positive association for one-child parents.
limitations: Review lists 2013 entry; subsequent papers also cite 2015 version. Do not count versions as independent datasets. Not country-specific result.
